description: every skipped test in the runtime suite, named and classified against the declared registry

skips.test: X03 regression: a leaked handle IS detected, and the POLARIS launcher leaks none
skips.reason: the /proc handle probe is a Linux-native check
skips.rationale: the probe reads /proc/self/fd to enumerate descriptors. That filesystem does not exist on Windows, so the instrument is platform-wrong there rather than the claim being unmeasured.
skips.windows_claim_carried_by: W-11 (X03 handle inheritance, native, with a positive control)

skips.test: a symbolic link that leaves the anchored root is caught after real resolution
skips.reason: junction creation needs a native Windows run
skips.rationale: the fixture builds a POSIX symlink to make a link that leaves the anchored root. On Windows the equivalent object is a directory junction, which the native runner creates and measures for real; the POSIX fixture would measure nothing there.
skips.windows_claim_carried_by: W-07 (junction escape detected as SYMLINK_ESCAPE) and W-06 (case-insensitive containment)

skips.test: containment is proven after link resolution, not before
skips.reason: junction creation needs a native Windows run
skips.rationale: the fixture builds a POSIX symlink to make a link that leaves the anchored root. On Windows the equivalent object is a directory junction, which the native runner creates and measures for real; the POSIX fixture would measure nothing there.
skips.windows_claim_carried_by: W-07 (junction escape detected as SYMLINK_ESCAPE) and W-06 (case-insensitive containment)

interpretation: class A is a platform-wrong instrument, B a case that does not exist on this platform, C an environment refusal of a measurable claim, D a security-critical claim left unmeasured. D and C block Phase-00 closure; an unclassified skip blocks it too, because an unnamed skip is indistinguishable from a hole.
